(`"2"` = mechanism directly observed empirically; `"1"` = documented statistical/descriptive association; `"0"` = inferred only by authors).

effect_estimate.comment: Binomial logistic regression odds ratios and p-values are reported separately for 2011 and 2023; 95% confidence intervals are not reported in the paper.
effect_estimate.value: In binomial logistic regressions of WASH absence across Brazilian rural public elementary schools in 2011 and 2023 (95% CIs not reported): (1) schools on Indigenous lands vs. non-differentiated rural areas had higher odds of lacking sanitation (OR = 5.58, p < 0.001 in 2011; OR = 5.48, p < 0.001 in 2023; prevalence 54.6% and 53.1% vs. 9.9% and 8.2%) and lacking toilets (OR = 8.82, p < 0.001 in 2011; OR = 4.55, p < 0.001 in 2023; prevalence 41.7% and 42.8% vs. 5.1% and 4.3%), with water absence on Indigenous lands rising from 6.0% to 13.2%; (2) very small schools (<=10 students vs. >50 students, linked by authors to per-student PDDE funding rules) had higher odds of lacking sanitation (OR = 4.97, p < 0.001 in 2011; OR = 2.73, p < 0.001 in 2023), lacking toilets (OR = 8.02, p < 0.001 in 2011; OR = 3.41, p < 0.001 in 2023), and in 2023 lacking water supply (OR = 2.28, p < 0.001); (3) North region schools (vs. Central-West) had elevated odds of lacking water (OR = 2.58, p < 0.001 in 2011; OR = 6.40, p < 0.001 in 2023), sanitation (OR = 3.32, p < 0.001 in 2011; OR = 5.48, p < 0.001 in 2023), and toilets in 2023 (OR = 5.17, p < 0.001; 2011 OR = 1.36, p = 0.143), while Northeast schools had elevated odds of lacking water (OR = 4.84, p < 0.001 in 2011; OR = 3.60, p < 0.001 in 2023); and (4) medium-sized municipalities (100,000-500,000 vs. >500,000 inhabitants) had higher odds of water absence in 2011 (OR = 4.48, p = 0.004).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF pp. 8-10, Tabela 1, Tabela 2, and Resultados (Fatores determinantes da ausência de WASH)
